clue.text: National emblem a counterfeit diamond?

parts.note: something counterfeit is a sham, a fake
rock is slang for a diamond

explanation.surface: A national symbol turns out to be a fake gem.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-leaved clover is the floral symbol of Ireland.

clue.text: Plain stuff from mixed shop menu

indicators.note: mixed tells us the letters of shop menu are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Ordinary goods turn up in a muddled shop's list.
explanation.definitionFit: Homespun cloth is plain, simple fabric woven at home.

clue.text: Cassandra, eg, producing original version of jabberwocky?

explanation.surface: A prophetess is credited with writing a nonsense poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Cassandra was the pen name of William Connor, columnist on the Daily Mirror newspaper; in Through the Looking-Glass, Alice first finds the Jabberwocky poem printed back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A columnist on the Daily Mirror paper, and someone producing reversed script readable only in a looking-glass.

clue.text: Such as should suit non-separatists

parts.note: a garment that is not made of separates, playing on separatists as political splitters

explanation.surface: Something to please those who oppose political separation.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimsuit or garment made as a single unit rather than separates top and bottom.

clue.text: Worked into ridges by the miller?

definitions.text: Worked into ridges by the miller?

parts.words: Worked into ridges by the miller?
parts.note: a coin's milled edge is ridged, so a miller's work gives that finish rather than flour

explanation.surface: A miller seems to have ploughed something into furrows.
explanation.definitionFit: Knurling is the milling of small ridges on metal, as on a coin edge or knob.

clue.text: Like a trampoline such poetic rhythm

explanation.surface: A bouncy mat is compared to verse.
explanation.walkthrough: Sprung rhythm is the metre devised by Gerard Manley Hopkins.
explanation.definitionFit: A trampoline has a mat held by springs; Hopkins named his stress-based verse metre this way.

clue.text: If I err, contrariwise, this decree could be invalidated

indicators.note: contrariwise asks for the phrase to be read the other way round, from end to start

parts.note: to err is to sin

explanation.surface: A judge muses that a ruling would collapse if a mistake had been made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contrariwise' turns I SIN (I err) back to front. A decree nisi in English divorce law is provisional, made absolute unless cause is shown against it.
explanation.definitionFit: A provisional court order that may still be set aside before it is made absolute.

clue.text: Grey, Richelieu's Private Secretary

parts.note: Père Joseph, the cardinal's adviser, was nicknamed for his grey friar's habit

explanation.surface: A man named Grey served as the cardinal's secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: The French title éminence grise, a power behind the throne, was first given to Richelieu's confidant Père Joseph.

clue.text: Preference that gets me in post improperly

indicators.note: improperly says the letters are arranged wrongly and must be put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone admits getting a job through favouritism.
explanation.definitionFit: Favouritism shown to relatives, especially in giving jobs.

clue.text: Tent-maker poet, O.K?

parts.note: the Persian poet whose surname means tent-maker has the initials O and K

explanation.surface: Asking whether a poet who makes tents is all right.
explanation.walkthrough: Khayyam means tent-maker in Persian; O.K. stands for the poet's initials, not approval.
explanation.definitionFit: The forename of Khayyam, the Persian poet of the Rubaiyat.

clue.text: After-effect of giving army corps drums etc

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
drums and other struck instruments make up the percussion section

explanation.surface: Consequences of handing a military unit drums.
explanation.definitionFit: A consequence or knock-on effect following an action.

clue.text: Extra pliant of mind

parts.note: pliant means supple, bending easily
mental means relating to the mind

explanation.surface: Someone is unusually flexible in thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Something supplemental is additional, added on.

clue.text: Boxes against egghead — by no means dense

parts.note: to box is to spar, so boxes gives spars
the head of egg is its first letter E

explanation.surface: Fighting an intellectual, who is anything but stupid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual but is the head of the word egg; 'against' just sets the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinly scattered is the opposite of thick or crowded.

clue.text: It's user may bear the yoke, say

definitions.text: It's user may bear the yoke, say

parts.words: It's user may bear the yoke, say
parts.note: yoke sounds like yolk, so the burden borne is egg rather than oxen's harness

explanation.surface: Someone carries a heavy yoke like a beast of burden.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spoon for eating a boiled egg, which carries the yellow centre.

clue.text: Reginald could become weather-beaten without one

indicators.note: could become says the letters may be rearranged into a new word

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Reginald might grow weathered without a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes I (one) from REGINALD, and 'could become' rearranges REGNALD.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnarled means knotted and rough, as worn by age and weather.

clue.text: Award for betrayal

explanation.surface: A prize given for treachery.
explanation.definitionFit: A free prize handed out, and a telltale sign revealing a secret.

clue.text: Art circle students behind bars

indicators.note: behind bars means locked inside, so the letters go within the word for bars

parts.note: a cage is made of bars
a circle is shaped like the letter O
L is a learner, so two learners give LL

explanation.surface: Art students sit in a circle, behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture made by sticking assorted materials onto a backing.

clue.text: Wells country

parts.note: not the cathedral city or H G Wells, but land full of oil wells

explanation.surface: The countryside around the city of Wells.
explanation.definitionFit: An area where crude petroleum is extracted from many bores.

clue.text: Ward representative

parts.note: not a councillor for an electoral district but someone acting for a child in their care

explanation.surface: A councillor representing an electoral district.
explanation.definitionFit: A person legally responsible for a minor acts on that ward's behalf.

clue.text: Ladies honoured to accept silver as compensation

indicators.note: to accept means the honoured ladies take the silver inside them

parts.note: a dame is a woman given a knighthood-level honour
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Decorated women receive silver as a payout.
explanation.definitionFit: Money awarded by a court for loss or injury.

clue.text: Stationed not quite plumb in the middle of London?

definitions.text: Stationed not quite plumb in the middle of London?

parts.words: Stationed not quite plumb in the middle of London?
parts.note: a main-line railway terminus in London, near but not exactly at its centre

explanation.surface: Something placed slightly off-centre in London.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria is a major London railway station in Westminster, near the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a central London railway terminus.

clue.text: See him among DIY in Yellow Pages, or in Crockford

definitions.text: See him among DIY in Yellow Pages, or in Crockford

parts.words: See him among DIY in Yellow Pages, or in Crockford
parts.note: put a parish priest between DI and Y to make the word for a listing such as Yellow Pages or Crockford's clerical list

explanation.surface: A clergyman looked up in a phone book among the do-it-yourself shops.
explanation.walkthrough: Crockford's Clerical Directory lists Church of England clergy; Yellow Pages is a business phone book.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish priest in the Church of England.

clue.text: At harvest-time this tide beat Sam back

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash

indicators.note: back says the name Sam is read in reverse

explanation.surface: At harvest someone gives Sam a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SAM into MAS. Lammas (1 August) is the old English harvest festival, and Lammastide its season.
explanation.definitionFit: The early-August loaf-mass festival marking the start of harvest.

clue.text: Increase in value of gratitude

explanation.surface: Prices rising and thanks given.
explanation.definitionFit: A rise in an asset's worth, and thankful recognition.

clue.text: This request sure to give satisfaction

definitions.text: This request sure to give satisfaction

parts.words: This request sure to give satisfaction
parts.note: the word for a request joined to the word sure forms a word meaning satisfaction

explanation.surface: A request certain to please.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest appeal or petition.

clue.text: Understand divining-rod

explanation.surface: Grasping how dowsing works.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for grasp or catch on, and a small forked branch used by dowsers.

clue.text: One acted out the story

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor performed the tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A short amusing tale of a real incident.

clue.text: Party row causes extra business

parts.note: a side is a party in a dispute or contest
a row is a line

explanation.surface: A political quarrel leads to a second job.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary occupation pursued alongside a main one.
